newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Nickel find sparks Dragon, Sons Gwalia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Nickel find sparks Dragon, Sons Gwalia.

text.p: Shares in Dragon Mining NL leapt over 50 percent to 17.5 cents, while Son of Gwalia scrip rebounded off its earlier bullion-depressed lows after the companies announced a nickel find in Western Australia.
Dragon said exploration work confirmed the presence of nickel at the Weld Range mine prospect with testing having revealed a broad mineralised envelope up to 60 metres thick.
The grading of the ore was above 0.5 percent nickel, including several intersections of greater than 1.00 percent and a top grade of 2.45 percent nickel, Dragon said.
"They have raced up after they came out with some very good results," said a Sydney-based resource analyst, adding that the report suggested further work may indicate stronger results to come.
"There is plenty of testing still to do but the results today are very encouraging. The grade is not incredibly high but they are wide intersections and are over such a large area."
The Weld Range prospect is 35 percent owned by Dragon and 65 percent by Sons of Gwalia.

By 3.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), Dragon shares were up 5.5 cents at A$0.17 on turnover of 21.8 million shares while Sons of Gwalia shares were eight cents higher at A$6.75, well off early lows of A$6.60, on turnover of 266,675 shares.
